title: Nano-surge lifecycle latency & cost vignette
content:
Purpose:
Quick exploratory vignette to capture qualitative and quantitative signals for very short-lived "nano" surges (1s-10s) and how different runtime configurations trade p50/p90/p99 latency against per-token cost under our console routing + fast-path heuristics. This is not a full bench report — its a working sketch to inform a short explainer card and a couple of dashboard widgets.

Context and motivation:
- Product asked: can we surface a single number that predicts the cost bump from a sudden 5–10s spike for interactive sessions?
- Ops: microbursts often drive p99/jank even when average costs are low; we need a concise narrative for the Console UI and a short-sla playbook.
- Assumption: workload = many short first-turns (50-150 tokens) with occasional multi-turn followups; 65% of requests are <200 tokens.

Test matrix (synthetic):
- Hardware: A100x2 equivalent (same cluster as recent console microbench).
- Model: M-small-8k (quantized), M-medium-16k (float32) as comparison points.
- Routing modes: fast-path (prefetch+tiling), multiplex (slotized), fallback (lower-capacity variant).
- Surge profile: 10k RPS sustained for 3s peak, baseline 500 RPS before/after.

Key measured metrics (aggregated across 5 runs):
- p50, p90, p99 generation latency (ms) for 1st token completion and end-to-end, and delta cost per 1M tokens in USD (approx).

ASCII summary table (median run):
Mode       | p50(ms)  | p90(ms)  | p99(ms)  | E2E mean(ms) | d$/1M tokens
---------------------------------------------------------------
fast-path  | 38       | 82       | 210      | 140          | +$26
multiplex  | 60       | 140      | 420      | 220          | +$18
fallback   | 45       | 95       | 650      | 190          | +$11

Quick observations:
- Fast-path wins p50/p90 and lowest end-to-end tail up to p90, but p99 still elevated (210ms) due to contention on KV cache refills during the first 1–2 tokens of many concurrent short sessions.
- Multiplex shows smoother cost per token (lower d$/1M) because of higher packing efficiency, but tail (p99) suffers when slot preemption and straggler requests align during the peak.
- Fallback to a lower-capacity variant reduces cost impact but dramatically increases worst-case tails when the model downgrade happens mid-session.

Tiny chart: surge vs p99 (relative units, run A)
Time(s):   0    1    2    3    4    5
p99 fast:  100  210  205  190  130  110
p99 mult:  120  320  400  380  200  140
p99 fall:  110  300  650  620  220  120
(visual takeaway: multiplex and fallback show higher peak p99 and longer recovery tail)

Cost-latency trade-off narrative (for an explainer blurb):
- If you prioritize steady UX (low p90) for short interactive queries, enable the fast-path preference; expect a modest cost bump during spikes due to prewarming and KV activity (+$20–$30 / 1M tokens for the synthetic microburst).
- If you prioritize minimizing incremental spend during spikes, prefer multiplex packing; you will save on token cost but accept higher p99 risk for the shortest interactions.
- Canary/fallback policies should avoid seamless downgrades mid-session; where possible, route new sessions to the lower-capacity variant rather than migrating live sessions.

Operational checklist (draft recommendations for Console widgets / runbooks):
- Add a "nano-surge" quick metric: max RPS over rolling 5s and immediate delta on p99 (5s window).
- Surface projected d$/1M tokens for the active routing policy in the top-right of the model route editor.
- Create an alert: if p99 increases >2x during a 5s window AND RPS spike >4x baseline, trigger a mitigation suggestion (switch to multiplex or pad fast-path pool).
- Provide a short tooltip: "fast-path = best p90, multiplex = best average cost under packing, fallback = cheapest token compute but worst p99 under migration".

Open questions / follow-ups (to resolve in full bench):
- How stable is the KV cache refill penalty across model sizes and longer context windows? We saw model-size amplification for M-medium-16k in follow-up runs.
- Is there a sweet-spot pad size for fast-path pool that cuts p99 excursions without raising baseline cost too much? Quick grid needed (pad 2/5/10%).
- Validate against real traffic trace (we used synthetic; next step: replay 24h of interactive sessions sampled from prod).

Notes to self / next steps:
- Convert this vignette into two deliverables: (1) a 1-page Console card with 3 bullets + micro-ASCII-chart, (2) a short-runbook with 3 mitigation steps and exact thresholds.
- Drop a link to this file in the model route PR and reference CNSL-8421.

Slack thread pointers: #console-metrics, #serving-runtime-bench.

Rough provenance: synthetic harness v0.9, bench script tag bench/nano-surge/v0.9, run id: ns-20290504-07 (see linked artifacts).

End of vignette.
